record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: For generic negatively curved compact Riemannian manifolds, do Laplace eigenfunctions φ_i have Gaussian value distribution, so that Vol({x∈X:a≤φ_i(x)≤b}) converges to (1/√(2π))∫_a^b exp(−t^2/2)dt as i→∞?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 52 (J. Marklof ). Vol({x ∈ X : a ≤ φi (x) ≤ b}) → 1/rad〉callow 2π ∫ b a e − t 2/2d t as i → ∞ .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, normalized so that $\mathrm{Vol}(X)=1$. Let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ denote an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of real-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $-\Delta_g$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i \to \infty$, and normalized so that $\int_X \varphi_i^2\,d\mathrm{Vol} = 1$.

Prove or disprove that for a generic such metric $g$, the values of the eigenfunctions are asymptotically Gaussian distributed with respect to the Riemannian volume; that is, for every pair of real numbers $a<b$,
$$\mathrm{Vol}\big(\{x\in X : a \le \varphi_i(x) \le b\}\big) \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}\,dt \qquad \text{as } i\to\infty.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is a form of Berry's random wave heuristic for eigenfunctions on negatively curved (or Anosov) manifolds. Recent work (e.g., Ingremeau's "Unimodal value distribution of Laplace eigenfunctions," 2019) establishes related partial results (such as unimodality of value distributions under a gradient-weighted measure and local weak Gaussian limits), but the full Gaussian value distribution under Riemannian volume remains an open conjecture for generic negatively curved compact manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Unimodal value distribution of Laplace eigenfunctions and a monotonicity formula
status_evidence.snippet: The random wave conjecture suggests that in certain situations, the value distribution of Laplace eigenfunctions under a Riemannian volume measure is approximately Gaussian.
status_evidence.claim: States the random wave/Gaussian value-distribution conjecture and proves only partial (unimodal) results.

status_evidence.title: Local Weak Limits of Laplace Eigenfunctions
status_evidence.snippet: Berry's conjecture should hold on any manifold of negative curvature (or more generally on manifolds whose geodesic flow is Anosov).
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the conjecture is expected to hold but is not proven for negatively curved manifolds.
